title: FinOps for Open-Banking Data Spend
one_liner: Bank data access is turning into a metered cost. Do for aggregator bills what cloud FinOps did for AWS bills.
customer: Fintech lenders, budgeting apps and payroll and EWA apps spending $200k-$10M per year on aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity) and direct bank APIs.
problem: The CFPB 1033 rule is stayed, and a rewrite sent to OIRA on 2026-08-06 may let banks charge aggregators past a free-request threshold (PYMNTS). Developers over-poll accounts and pay per connection and per refresh, and a fee threshold would create sudden bill shock. Nobody owns the cost line.
solution: A proxy and observability layer that dedupes and caches pulls, replaces polling with webhooks and event-based refreshes, refreshes only when a decision needs fresh data (underwriting, payday), benchmarks vendor mix and price, and forecasts spend under proposed fee scenarios.
why_now: Regulatory uncertainty is at its peak, states like New York are proposing their own regimes, and fintechs face margin pressure. Any fee threshold in the rewrite turns data access into variable cost of goods sold.
revenue_model: 15-20% of verified savings (gainshare) or $2k-$10k per month SaaS.
non_obvious_insight: Data-access cost is becoming a real COGS line that finance teams can't yet see. My hypothesis is that dedupe and smarter refresh timing alone save 20-40%, so the first step is an audit that verifies it. A fee threshold makes that savings pool bigger.
first_30_days: Offer a free aggregator bill audit to 20 fintechs (they share invoices and usage exports). Quantify wasteful pulls, convert two to a 15% gainshare agreement, and publish the anonymized benchmark.

title: Phage Red-Teaming and Immunity Stacks for Fermenters
one_liner: Penetration-test production strains with adversarially evolved phages, then harden them with stacked, AI-selected anti-phage defenses.
customer: Industrial fermentation operators and CDMOs running E. coli, Bacillus, Corynebacterium or Streptomyces hosts for recombinant proteins, enzymes, amino acids and precision-fermentation ingredients.
problem: Phage contamination can cause widespread fermentation failure and lingering facility contamination, and outages are usually hidden. Dairy lactic-acid strains have phage-resistance programs, but most other production hosts do not. Academic work shows phage-resistant E. coli is feasible (Nature Communications 2022; CRISPR-immunity work in 2025), yet nobody sells it as a service.
solution: (1) Surveillance: metagenomic sequencing of broth and environmental swabs for phage signatures. (2) Red team: isolate and evolve escape phages against the customer's strain in a BSL-1/2 lab, extending the search with AI-designed phage genomes. (3) Hardening: stack defense modules (restriction-modification, CRISPR, abortive infection), test them, and deliver a strain with unchanged titer.
why_now: Arc Institute and Stanford used Evo genome language models to write phage genomes: 16 viable phages from about 300 designs, and a cocktail that cleared E. coli resistant to the natural template. DNA synthesis costs have collapsed, so testing dozens of defense combinations is cheap. Precision fermentation and biologic capacity is scaling.
revenue_model: $2-6k/month per site for surveillance, $25-60k per red-team audit, and $150-400k per hardened strain as a license fee without royalties.
non_obvious_insight: Phage risk is treated as bad luck. Treating it like cybersecurity, with continuous monitoring plus adversarial testing, creates a budget line. Operators hide outages, so the first buyers are CDMO QA leads and insurers who need proof of resilience.
first_30_days: Offer a free phage-susceptibility screen of environmental swabs to 5 precision-fermentation startups. Build a library of 30 defense modules for E. coli and Bacillus. Sign 2 paid audits ($15-25k). Complete a biosafety review of the adversarial-phage protocol.

title: Contingency Refunds for Fake Local-Service Leads
one_liner: A win-based service that audits what plumbers, HVAC firms, locksmiths, law offices and clinics pay per lead or call, proves which were bots, spam or out-of-area, and files the platform disputes owners never get around to.
customer: Owner-operators of 1-20 person home-service, legal and clinic businesses spending $1.5K-15K/month on Google Local Services Ads, Thumbtack, Angi, Yelp and tracked call numbers. Fee is 25% of credits recovered.
problem: 'Reaching customers' is the number-one small-business challenge (Fed SBCS 2026) while legacy local-marketing vendors shrink (Thryv 2025 revenue $785M, down). Owners pay per lead but cannot tell real jobs from junk, and platform dispute windows are short and evidence-heavy, so credits likely go unclaimed (my inference; recovery rates need testing). Bot share of web traffic is estimated anywhere from about 20% (Cloudflare CEO) to over 50% (Imperva/Fortune), and cheap AI voice agents make robo-calls to paid numbers easier.
solution: The owner connects ad and lead accounts or forwards lead emails and call-tracking numbers. The system transcribes calls, scores caller numbers, checks geography and duplicates, classifies wrong-service and spam leads, and flags synthetic voices. It assembles evidence and files disputes inside each platform's window, reconciles the credits, and reports a monthly verified-lead rate per channel to guide budget.
why_now: Speech-to-text and classification now cost pennies per call. AI-generated traffic is polluting pay-per-lead channels while platform-native verification stays thin. Small owners have less time and money than ever, and outcome-priced recovery is exactly what subscription incumbents cannot easily offer.
revenue_model: 25% of credits recovered, plus a $49/month scorecard after month 3. Later add white-label to marketing agencies and sell verified-lead-rate benchmarks.
non_obvious_insight: Platforms already built refund mechanisms and profit from friction, so packaging evidence on time is the whole product. The independent verified-lead rate per channel is the first honest ROI data most SMBs ever get, and it may end up worth more than the refunds. Contingency pricing works because credits appear as visible cash in the ad account.
first_30_days: Recruit 15 owners from HVAC, garage-door, locksmith and plumber Facebook groups with a free 60-day lookback audit. Contract VAs to file disputes manually and measure recovery as a percent of spend. Publish a junk-lead-rate benchmark by platform, and build software only once recovery exceeds roughly 8% of spend.

title: The Unrecorded Room
one_liner: Hourly, certified no-recording rooms (phone lockers, no AI notetakers, analog paper only) for conversations too candid to survive a transcript.
customer: General counsels and outside counsel, boards and special committees, M&A and restructuring teams, VC-founder negotiations, HR investigators, and labor-management negotiators in one dense business district. They pay $200-400/hour or $2-5k/month firm memberships.
problem: AI notetakers now sit in most meetings. In mid-2026 firms such as Mayer Brown were warning that they create discoverable transcripts and privilege risk, and in February 2026 Judge Rakoff (SDNY) held that a defendant's chats with an AI platform were not privileged. Virtual meetings can't be sealed. Even offices are full of transcribing laptops, smart speakers, and phones. Leaders' workaround is 'let's take a walk'.
solution: Rooms with phone and laptop lockers, RF-shielded walls, whiteboards and paper pads, and a sign-in ritual. All attendees sign an 'Unrecorded' attestation that no recording or AI tool is in use. The venue logs who attended, never what was said. It offers concierge booking and a 'war room' day package. Counsel reviews the model so the room never destroys existing records, only avoids creating new ones. Later it certifies hotel suites and law-firm floors as 'Unrecorded Certified'.
why_now: AI notetaker penetration is high, and 2026 legal commentary and case law make the privilege and discovery risk concrete. The person paying is the person personally liable for the record.
revenue_model: Hourly room fees, firm memberships, and day-long war-room packages ($3k). White-label and certification fees from hotels and law-firm floors.
non_obvious_insight: In a fully transcribed world, the provable absence of a record is a premium product, and the buyer is the person with legal liability. Invitation to the unrecorded room becomes a high-trust status marker. It is a venue business that is not competing with coworking, because it sells evidence that nothing was kept.
first_30_days: Lease 3-4 rooms inside an existing coworking or law-office building on revenue share. Give CLE talks at the local bar association on 'AI notetakers and privilege' as a cheap lead engine. Have a TSCM consultant validate a low-cost shielding and locker setup. Pre-sell 10 firm memberships.

title: Live Doom-Pile Sessions for Avoided Paperwork
one_liner: A scheduled video session where a calm, admin-savvy host sits with you while you open the unopened mail pile, triages it, and gets the scary items handled before you hang up.
customer: Adults 25-55 with ADHD, anxiety, depression, recent bereavement or new-parent overload pay $59 per session or $89 a month for two sessions. Employer benefit programs, credit unions and probate attorneys pay for seats.
problem: Millions of people leave envelopes and portal notifications unopened because not knowing is more comfortable than knowing. Late fees, collections, missed renewals and tax notices escalate. The avoidance is emotional, so productivity apps and reminder tools do not touch it.
solution: A 45-minute weekly 'Admin Sunday' session. Members upload photos of the pile beforehand and AI produces a triage card (ignore, do this month, act by Friday). A trained host, such as a former paralegal, bookkeeper or benefits caseworker, sits with the member on camera as each envelope is opened. Three actions get done in the session, such as calling with a script, setting up a payment plan, or filing a form. The member leaves with a 'Nothing Scary' summary. A mail-forwarding tier serves people who cannot face even the session.
why_now: Adult ADHD diagnoses have surged and body-doubling is mainstream on TikTok and in tools like Focusmate. LLMs make triage and drafting nearly free, so one human can run 6-8 sessions a day and the business keeps a healthy margin. Collections on federal student loans restarted in 2025, raising the stakes of ignored mail. Consumers now value human presence precisely because AI can read the letter but cannot sit next to you.
revenue_model: $89 monthly subscription for two sessions, $59 a la carte. Hosts are paid $28-35 an hour, giving roughly 55-60% gross margin. B2B seats at $12-20 per employee per month for EAP and financial-wellness buyers.
non_obvious_insight: The product is courage with a witness, not productivity. People will pay to discover bad news in the company of someone calm. Silent co-working apps do not solve this because the body double is not allowed to help, and AI alone cannot absorb the emotion of opening the envelope.
first_30_days: Post in ADHD and adulting communities and make short 'doom pile' videos. Run 10 free consented live sessions to create content and testimonials. Sell $49 founding-member sessions through Stripe and run on Zoom and Google Drive. Recruit 5 hosts from retired paralegal and bookkeeper groups. Goal: 15 paying subscribers by day 30 and 30 by day 60.

title: Flooded Homeowners Meet Wetland Mitigation Buyers
one_liner: Match repeatedly flooded homeowners who want out with wetland and stream mitigation bankers who need floodplain land and can pay faster than federal buyouts.
customer: Compensatory-mitigation bankers, in-lieu-fee programs and land trusts (acquisition fee), counties and cities with repetitive-loss properties (program-management contracts), and homeowners (free, receive offers).
problem: Federal buyouts take years, and funding has become unreliable since the 2025 cancellation of BRIC and subsequent court fights. Meanwhile flood insurance premiums keep rising under Risk Rating 2.0 and repeat-flood homes are hard to sell. Mitigation bankers must buy contiguous floodplain and riparian land to earn Clean Water Act credits but usually source rural farmland by landman. They do not see suburban stream corridors lined with flooded homes as inventory.
solution: Screen NFIP repetitive-loss data, lidar and flood models and the RIBITS bank and credit ledger to find stream reaches where clusters of repeat-flood parcels adjoin high-credit-price watersheds. Run homeowner outreach and assemble willing sellers into a single package for a banker or land trust. The homes are demolished and the floodplain restored, with credits sold to permit-seeking developers and transport agencies.
why_now: Federal buyout money is slow and unpredictable, insurance repricing keeps rising, and data-center, industrial and transport permitting is driving demand for Section 404 mitigation credits. Public flood, lidar and ledger data make cluster screening possible for a small team.
revenue_model: Success fee of 2% to 3% of purchase price or $10k to $25k per assembled cluster (via a licensed real-estate partner), $2k to $5k a month screening subscription for bankers, and $50k to $150k municipal program-management contracts.
non_obvious_insight: A chain of flooded houses is exactly the restoration real estate a mitigation banker cannot otherwise get, and the funder of last resort can be a regulated compliance market rather than the taxpayer. This is a Clean Water Act compliance market, not a voluntary carbon-style offset.
first_30_days: Map 50 candidate reaches from public repetitive-loss, lidar and RIBITS data. Call 10 bankers and land trusts with a shopping list. Mail 200 homeowners on one reach. Sign a pilot with one banker and one county for program management.

title: Cross-Border Income Passport for Freelancers
one_liner: Give stablecoin-paid remote workers a verifiable, portable income record that landlords, lenders and visa agents accept.
customer: Freelancers and remote workers in Nigeria, the Philippines, Colombia and Kenya; landlords, lenders and visa agents pay to verify.
problem: Freelancers cannot get portable income records for loans or visas, and stablecoin and platform-wallet earnings leave no bank paper trail.
solution: Connect wallets, payout platforms and invoices, then produce signed income attestations with a QR verification link. The wedge is rental and visa income letters at about $15 each for remote workers in Lagos and Manila.
why_now: Stablecoin payroll and invoicing tools like Bloccpay are spreading, Flutterwave and Yellow Card are scaling, and LatAm lenders are hunting for new borrowers.
revenue_model: $10-20 per attestation, plus $1-3 per verification call from lenders.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck in stablecoin income is proving it, not moving it. Whoever gets accepted by three lenders becomes a bureau for the remote-work diaspora.
first_30_days: Build attestations from Payoneer, Wise and USDC statements and test with 50 workers and one landlord network.

title: Contingency Subrogation Forensics for Robot Accidents
one_liner: CCC-for-robots: a forensic recovery shop that turns warehouse-robot, AV and drone logs into fault-apportioned recovery demands for the insurers who already paid the claim.
customer: Subrogation units and TPAs at mid-size commercial P&C carriers, warehouse-focused MGAs, and brokers serving 3PLs and logistics parks.
problem: Robots damage racking, inventory, vehicles and people, and the insurer pays first, often under a policy never rated for robots. Recovery depends on whether the hardware, the model, the integrator's configuration, the operator's procedure or maintenance failed. The evidence sits in vendor-controlled logs and cloud consoles that get purged, and vendor contracts cap liability and force arbitration. Adjusters do not know what to ask for or how fast.
solution: A standard 72-hour evidence-preservation and vendor data-request package. Log parsers for the export formats of 3-5 common AMR, AGV, forklift and robotaxi platforms. A reconstruction timeline. A fault-apportionment matrix (OEM, integrator, operator, maintainer, site) with contract-cap analysis, plus a demand package addressed to the vendor's insurer.
why_now: Warehouse robot fleets, many of them imported, are scaling faster than underwriters' understanding, and trade press says insurers are unprepared. Robotaxi fleets are expanding across US cities in 2026. Carriers adding AI exclusions to GL, E&O and EPLI make 'which policy pays' a live dispute, which raises the value of recovering the loss from someone else. Claims from 2024-25 deployments are now maturing into subrogation files.
revenue_model: $3-8k flat fee per file plus 15-25% contingency on recoveries above a threshold. Later, annual retainers with carriers and a licensed evidence-request tool for adjusters.
non_obvious_insight: The first real price of AI and robot liability will be set in recovery negotiations, not in underwriting. Whoever standardises how blame is split between OEM, integrator and operator, and holds the resulting loss-cost data, becomes the rating bureau, as CCC and Verisk did in auto. The bottleneck is evidence access and speed, not legal theory.
first_30_days: Email 30 subrogation managers and TPAs offering a free reconstruction and recovery memo on one closed robot or AV claim within 10 days. Bring on an ex-robotics field-service engineer and subrogation counsel on a retainer. Write the preservation-letter pack. Aim for 2 paid files by day 60.

title: Approved-Protocol Envelope Guard for AI-Directed Labs
one_liner: Middleware that turns an institution's biosafety approval into machine-readable limits and stops any agent-proposed experiment that falls outside them before a robot runs it, leaving an insurer-grade black-box record.
customer: Biosafety officers and lab directors at universities, CROs and AI-native biotechs that let agents propose or modify protocols. Later, insurers and MGAs who need trace data. The direct buyer is the lab or institution.
problem: Institutional Biosafety Committees approve specific organisms, agents, quantities and containment levels, but agents now propose edits on the fly (a new strain, a higher concentration, a substitute reagent). There is no standard sign-off model, since CDC/WHO frameworks predate autonomous systems, and records must separate AI proposal, human edit and robot execution. ISO's generative-AI exclusion (CG 40 47 01 26) took effect in January 2026 and Verisk is weighing agentic exclusions, so the resulting liability is increasingly uninsured.
solution: Ingest the approved protocol (IBC registration, BSL level, permitted agents and amounts, IACUC limits) as a machine-readable envelope. Check every agent-proposed step against it before execution. Anything out of envelope pauses the run and goes to the biosafety officer with a diff. All proposals, human edits and executions are logged tamper-evidently. Each run yields an 'envelope compliance report' for the IBC file and, later, for underwriters.
why_now: Anthropic's wet lab and similar setups (about 950 agents on one discovery) show agents can generate far more proposals than human reviewers can read. The FDA's September 2026 nonclinical-methods rule raises scrutiny of AI-run studies. Carriers are excluding what they cannot model, so trace holders can price the risk.
revenue_model: SaaS per lab or robot ($1-3K/month), enterprise deployments for CROs, and later an MGA or data-licensing arrangement in which underwriters pay for envelope-compliance telemetry or grant premium credits.
non_obvious_insight: The real buyer is the overloaded biosafety officer, not the scientist, and the hard part is translating IBC PDFs into constraints rather than the AI. Whoever holds the runtime traces becomes the pricing authority for agentic lab risk, and model labs cannot be that neutral party.
first_30_days: Interview 15 biosafety officers through the ABSA community. Ship a read-only 'diff checker' that takes an IBC protocol PDF plus an agent's experiment plan and flags out-of-envelope steps. Sell 3 paid pilots ($2-5K) to AI-native labs and one university core. Use the pilot logs to draft an insurer-ready report format.

title: Friday Programs for Four-Day School Districts
one_liner: A turnkey 'fifth-day' care and enrichment operator that runs in existing school buildings for districts on four-day weeks, funded by parent fees and vouchers.
customer: Rural and small-town districts on four-day weeks (hundreds of districts across 20+ states, from memory) and their working parents. Also 21st CCLC and state after-school grant programs.
problem: Districts adopted four-day weeks to cut costs and recruit teachers. The off day leaves working parents with no care in places where licensed slots are already scarce, so kids stay alone, with grandparents or parents leave jobs. Each district improvises its own Friday program.
solution: An operating kit: a staffing pool (education majors and retired teachers), background-check pipeline, daily curriculum, parent sign-up and payment, subsidy-voucher billing, insurance and transport. The district provides the building. We run the first sites ourselves, then license the kit for a management fee.
why_now: ESSER money ended, so more districts are trimming days (from memory). Childcare prices are up 29% since 2020 and rural supply is thin. CCDF rules moving to enrollment-based payment help small operators get paid reliably.
revenue_model: Parent fee of $35-50 per child per day, with a 15% management fee or per-site licence when franchised to local operators. Voucher billing adds funded slots.
non_obvious_insight: This desert is a day-of-week desert created by a policy choice, and the most expensive input (the building) is already paid for by taxpayers. That makes the unit economics better than standard childcare.
first_30_days: Call 20 four-day-week districts in Missouri, Oklahoma and Colorado. Run one paid pilot Friday with 15-25 kids at $40 a day. Recruit staff from the nearest college's education program. Track true margin per child-day and use the data to sell the second district.

title: Data Center Deal Desk for Rural Counties
one_liner: An independent negotiating desk that gives county and township boards a benchmark of every comparable data-center abatement and community-benefit contract, a counter term sheet and a fiscal model, paid for by the developer's review escrow.
customer: County commissions, township boards, school boards and local economic-development authorities facing data-center proposals, plus state associations of counties and resident coalitions.
problem: Developers have negotiated dozens of deals and arrive with NDAs and shell LLCs. Counties have negotiated none, and commissioners vote on abatements they can't benchmark. Leverage disappears once approvals are granted. Terms on water use, noise, diesel backup hours, decommissioning bonds, grid-cost protection and clawbacks vary wildly.
solution: Parse every signed abatement, PILOT, host-community and large-load utility agreement obtainable (the Federation of American Scientists started collecting signed agreements in early 2026, and public records requests fill gaps) into a comparable clause database. Deliver a two-week Deal Review: where each term falls against the median and best deals, a counter term sheet, fiscal, water and power impact modeling, and a 'second chair' during meetings. Fees are typically recoverable from the applicant through a third-party review escrow.
why_now: The 2026 data-center land rush has local governments scrambling: most local ordinances and ballot measures tracked in 2026 passed, many deals sit behind NDAs, and counties from Texas to Ohio are tabling or denying abatements while others approve blind. LLMs make reading hundreds of messy contracts cheap. Incumbent consultants and county attorneys don't have a comparables dataset.
revenue_model: $12k to $40k per deal review (billed to the developer's review escrow where the county allows it), annual data license for state county associations ($30k to $100k) and, later, a pre-vetted 'fast-lane' term sheet that developers pay to use.
non_obvious_insight: Information asymmetry, not law, is the county's problem, and the cheapest fix is a set of comparables. Commissioners also fear being first or being fleeced, so 'we asked for what the median county got' gives political cover. Charging the applicant through the review escrow means the buyer, a cash-strapped county, doesn't need a budget line.
first_30_days: Collect 100 signed agreements from the FAS repository, Texas Chapter 312 filings and records requests, and code them into a comparison table. Publish free state scorecards. Email commissioners in counties with pending abatement votes and offer a $5k rapid clause redline, asking the county to request that the developer pay under its review-fee ordinance.

title: AI Coverage Buy-Back Packs for Insurance Agents
one_liner: An intake that turns a small business's AI usage into an underwriter-ready 'AI use and guardrails' package so its insurer will restore the coverage it just excluded.
customer: Independent insurance agencies and brokerages that serve SMBs, who pay per client pack or a monthly agency subscription. Their clients are marketing agencies, law and accounting firms, clinics, staffing firms and e-commerce brands that use AI heavily.
problem: ISO endorsements CG 40 47 and CG 40 48 took effect in January 2026 and let carriers exclude generative-AI-related bodily injury, property damage and advertising injury from standard general liability policies. Reporting says Chubb, Travelers and Berkshire Hathaway got state approvals, and more than 80% of such requests were approved. Absolute AI exclusions are also appearing on D&O and E&O policies, including for 'allegedly inadequate AI governance'. About 74% of small businesses already use AI tools, and agents cannot tell clients what evidence underwriters will accept.
solution: A 15-minute intake, plus an optional SSO or browser scan, inventories the client's AI tools. It maps each use (customer chatbot, AI-generated ads, AI hiring screens, AI note-takers with client data) to the coverage lines it touches. It then produces: (1) a coverage-gap report that flags CG 40 47/48 and absolute AI exclusions in the current policy, (2) an underwriter-ready AI use and guardrails statement with a human-review log and vendor list, and (3) a quote-request package aimed at markets that sell affirmative AI coverage or buy-backs. Every pack also gives the agent a talk track for the renewal meeting.
why_now: The exclusions have been in effect since January 2026 and are now hitting renewals. Search interest is rising in the underlying concepts: Exploding Topics shows AI Guardrails +8,400%, Responsible AI +3,600% and Cyber Insurance +763%. Colorado's AI Act, delayed to Jan 1, 2027, and Illinois HB 3773 (in effect Jan 1, 2026) add employer-side documentation duties that the same pack can reuse.
revenue_model: $149-$299 per client pack, or $199-$499/month per agency for unlimited packs plus renewal reminders. Later: a referral or placement fee from managing general agents and carriers that write AI buy-backs, and a co-branded version sold through carrier appointment programs.
non_obvious_insight: The evidence standard does not exist yet. Law firm analyses of the exclusions note they 'stop short of prescribing specific governance standards insurers will accept' (https://www.lathropgpm.com/insights/the-ai-coverage-gap-what-new-insurance-exclusions-mean-for-your-business/) and describe fragmenting coverage across GL, D&O, E&O and EPLI (https://www.fenwick.com/insights/publications/end-silent-ai-emerging-ai-exclusions-coverage-fragmentation-and-practical-implications). Whichever evidence format two or three underwriters or MGAs accept first will become the SOC 2 of AI coverage. Agents, not the businesses themselves, are the right buyer because they lose commission if a client goes bare. Cyber-insurance search interest is up 763% and AI Guardrails up 8,400% (https://explodingtopics.com/finance-topics, https://explodingtopics.com/blog/trending-topics), which shows SMBs are already looking for this without a product to buy.
first_30_days: Days 1-10: build the intake form and PDF generator, and interview 15 independent agents (local IIABA and Big I chapters, LinkedIn) about how renewals with AI exclusions are being handled. Days 11-20: run free packs for each agent's five most AI-heavy clients, and ask two MGA underwriters whether the format is acceptable. Days 21-30: start charging $149 per pack. Target 5 agencies at $199/month and post 'we got X's AI coverage bought back' cases from the pilots.

title: On-Demand Human Witnesses for Scrap and Recycled Claims
one_liner: A network of trained, insured, credentialed ex-auditors and QA people who can be dispatched within 24 hours to physically inspect scrap lots and witness recycled-content claims, producing tamper-evident signed reports.
customer: Remote buyers of bales and scrap lots (PET reclaimers, black-mass and tungsten buyers, brokers, traders). Brands making recycled-content claims, and their insurers and lenders. The buyers' own AI purchasing agents consume the reports through an API.
problem: PET bales trade at a record-low 1.44 c/lb while food-grade supply is called constrained, which points to a quality-tier mismatch nobody can see without inspection. Generative AI makes photos, scale tickets and certificates trivially forgeable. Traditional inspectors have minimum fees and multi-day lead times. Mass-balance claims are contested and no standard exists. California's AB 2253 (claim substantiation) was vetoed, leaving brands exposed to litigation. EU rules banning generic green claims (Directive 2024/825) began applying on Sept 27, 2026.
solution: Recruit displaced auditors, QA analysts, supply-chain and compliance staff and give them a one-day protocol course on bale and scrap specs. Dispatch them to open and grade bales, XRF-screen metals, seal loads, witness weigh-outs and attend recycled-content production runs. They use a capture app with device attestation and signed provenance, and every report is machine-readable. Visits cost $95-250 versus $800+ for traditional inspection. Each witness builds a portable, scored reputation, so the credential becomes their asset.
why_now: AI forgery capability is now cheap and widely known, so document trust is falling. The BIS Aug 27 rule adds recordkeeping for black mass and tungsten scrap. Brands need substantiation now that the EU rules apply. Agentic procurement needs verifiable physical inputs. The supply of trained auditors and analysts is growing because of AI-driven cuts.
revenue_model: Per-inspection fee split about 60/40 with the witness. Monthly claim-assurance subscriptions for brands ($1-3K). API and report-verification fees for buyers' agents. Later, a quality-tier index of bales sold to the market.
non_obvious_insight: When AI can fake any document, the scarce commodity is a credentialed human who was physically present. The scrap trade runs on thin margins and unverifiable quality claims, so cheap, fast human presence beats expensive certification. AI displacement supplies the witnesses at the same moment it destroys trust in paperwork.
first_30_days: Pick one corridor with several bale or e-scrap buyers and offer 20 discounted bale inspections to three remote buyers. Recruit and train 10 witnesses (ex-QA and audit). Build the capture flow on existing attestation and C2PA tools. Publish a first bale-quality report from the results.

title: Inverter-Telemetry Credit Bureau for African Solar
one_liner: Turn the cloud data that hybrid inverters and batteries already stream into a consented energy cash-flow score, so lenders, insurers and installers can finance an asset boom that official statistics cannot see.
customer: Solar and battery asset financiers, MFIs and banks in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, plus installers who need financing to close sales. Insurers and DFIs paying for verified performance come later.
problem: Africa installs 17 GW of solar in 2026 (+45%), 75% of the growth is distributed, and it imports more battery dollars than panels. Ember says its estimates are 2x official figures and only 14 of 54 countries reported 2025 data, so credit bureaus and insurers have nothing to price on. Installers cannot get customers financed, and lenders cannot see collateral health or borrower activity.
solution: With owner consent gathered through the installer, pull production, load, battery health, uptime and location data from inverter and BMS clouds (Victron VRM, Solarman for Deye, Growatt, Huawei, Solis). Compute diesel displacement and savings, a load-profile proxy for business activity (cold-room cycles, salon hours), collateral health and tamper flags, and installer quality scores. Sell an API and dashboard to lenders, with remote-lock hooks and insurer feeds as add-ons.
why_now: Distributed solar plus batteries has become private infrastructure. Stationary packs fell 45% to about $70/kWh, African equity funding is concentrated while debt replaces equity (so lenders need collateral visibility), and India's UPI fee change shows how fragile transaction-data underwriting is. The US also needs neutral telemetry, since Sunrun and Tesla's 16.8 GW capacity-as-a-service has no disclosed verification standard.
revenue_model: $2-6 per scored asset per month or per-report fees, a 1-2% origination fee on financing it unlocks, installer SaaS, insurer data licensing, and later verification fees from results-based financing programs.
non_obvious_insight: The best alternative-credit dataset in Africa is already being emitted by hardware nobody thinks of as a bureau. Energy consumption is a real-time proxy for small-business activity, and the inverter is both the collateral and the sensor. Because the data layer is vendor-neutral, it can later certify firm distributed capacity for utilities and hyperscalers, something Tesla and Enphase cannot credibly do for each other's fleets.
first_30_days: Integrate two APIs (Victron VRM and Solarman/Deye) and sign 3 installers in Lagos, Nairobi or Johannesburg with 300+ systems between them. Collect customer consents through the installers' apps and publish a free installed-base map. Take the top-scoring 30 customers to one MFI or asset financier for a pilot loan pool, charging a 2% origination fee.

title: Presence Ledger: Reconstruct Every Trip You Took
one_liner: Ingests flight emails, CBP I-94 history, location exports and passport stamps to produce an evidence-backed, officer-proof travel table for naturalization, green-card retention and tax residency.
customer: Immigration law firms (per-client fee), CPAs and tax preparers serving foreign nationals (Form 8843/substantial presence test), HR mobility teams, and green card holders or naturalization applicants directly.
problem: N-400 applicants must list every trip of 24 hours or more in the past 5 years with exact dates. Almost no one can. Officers compare the list with CBP entry and exit records, and an honest gap or mismatch turns an interview into a good-moral-character or false-testimony problem. Green card holders with long absences risk a presumption of broken continuous residence, and scrutiny of returning residents at ports of entry has risen. The same reconstruction is needed for IRS substantial presence day counts, state tax residency audits, and Schengen/UK day counts. Paralegals spend 1-3 hours per client pulling this together by hand, and it is still wrong.
solution: A consent-based tool that pulls the official CBP I-94 travel history, scans Gmail/Outlook for airline and hotel confirmations, ingests Google Timeline or phone location exports and card transactions, and OCRs photos of passport stamps. It reconciles them into a single timeline with confidence flags, asks the user only about unresolved gaps, and exports (a) an N-400-style trip table with the proof behind each row, (b) day counts for physical presence, substantial presence and Schengen limits, and (c) a warning when a planned trip would cross a risk threshold (for example 180 days, or a trip that would break continuous residence).
why_now: Naturalization is being scrutinized more heavily in 2025-26, with a new civics test, a renewed focus on good moral character and reinstated neighborhood-style inquiries. Border stops of returning residents are up. Remote and hybrid work has multiplied cross-border days and tax exposure. Location data is now easy to export from phones, and LLMs make email and stamp parsing cheap enough for a small team to build in weeks.
revenue_model: $49-79 per case billed to law firms (white-label), $29-49 self-serve for applicants, $12-20 per client for CPAs during tax season, and a $9/month subscription for green card holders who want ongoing day tracking and pre-trip risk checks.
non_obvious_insight: The danger is not the trips you forget but the mismatch between your list and what the government already holds. A trip table with attached proof, pre-reconciled against CBP's own record, changes the tone of an interview. The exact same dataset is what tax audits and residency disputes need, so an immigration wedge opens a much larger tax-residency market with no extra data collection.
first_30_days: Build only the N-400 5-year trip table with I-94 history import plus email parsing. Give it free to 10 immigration firms in exchange for a testimonial and a comparison against their manual tables. Charge $49 from client number 11 on. Post the before/after error rates from real cases. In parallel, offer a $15 8843/substantial-presence day-count report through 5 CPAs who serve OPT/H-1B clients.

title: Listing Bodyguard: Scam-Listing Takedown for Property Managers
one_liner: Continuously scans the web for scam copies of a property manager's listings and takes them down, and gives real prospects a fast way to verify that a listing is legitimate.
customer: Property managers and leasing companies with 100 to 3,000 units, paying a monthly subscription. The buyer is the marketing or leasing director. Secondary buyers are apartment associations, large landlords' insurers and rental listing portals.
problem: Scammers copy a manager's real listing photos, undercut the rent by 25 to 40% and collect application fees and deposits from victims who never see the unit. Victims then show up at the property or call the leasing office furious, and often leave one-star reviews of the real manager. Real leads are poached by the fake listing, and the leasing team wastes hours on angry callers and manual takedown requests to Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace and others. There is no owner of the problem: the listing platforms are slow, police shrug and the PM's syndication vendor does not monitor. AI now makes it trivial to generate thousands of fake listings, with photos rewritten and descriptions localized.
solution: Pull each PM's live listing feed (from the syndication export in AppFolio, Buildium, Yardi or RentManager), compute perceptual hashes of every photo and fingerprints of the description text and address, then continuously search for matches across Craigslist, Zillow-family sites, Facebook (through allowed methods and user reports), OfferUp and the open web through reverse-image APIs. When a match appears on a listing whose contact does not belong to the PM, the system files takedown requests through each platform's copyright, fraud or impersonation channel with evidence, tracks status, and escalates. Prevention layer: every real listing gets a short verification code ('Verify: text 4471 to our verified line'), and a landing page confirms the unit and the real contact, giving prospects a free way to check before wiring money. Weekly reports show scams blocked, leads protected and estimated victim exposure.
why_now: Generative AI made scam listings cheap and scalable in 2025 and 2026, and consumer-protection agencies continue to list rental scams among the top fraud categories. Rental portals are under pressure to verify but are slow. The reverse-image and vision APIs from major providers make similarity search inexpensive, and the takedown channels are already documented, so a small team can automate a job that leasing staff currently do by hand.
revenue_model: $0.50 to $1.50 per active listing per month with a $199 monthly minimum, or a flat tier for portfolios. Upsell: white-label verification pages and analytics for apartment associations, and API licensing to listing portals and insurers who want fewer fraud claims.
non_obvious_insight: To a leasing office, a scam listing is not a consumer-fraud story. It is a top-of-funnel leak and a brand problem, because the scammer steals real leads and the victims blame the PM. Managers already know this but treat it as a nuisance, so there is a budget for a fix but no product. The real moat is the takedown playbook per platform: which channel, which wording, which contact person actually gets a listing removed within hours rather than days.
first_30_days: Manually audit 3 to 5 friendly PMs: take their public listings, run reverse-image searches and show them the scam copies already live (there will be some). That audit is the sales pitch, and most PMs have never looked. Build a script using Google Vision web-detection or TinEye plus Craigslist and Marketplace searches for a first pass, and a shared dashboard for takedown status. Charge $199 per month per portfolio starting in month 2. Ask each PM for a testimonial and a 'stopped 14 scams last quarter' number to bring to the next landlord association talk.

title: Immune-Graded Beef-on-Dairy Calves With Warranty
one_liner: A $1 refractometer reading at day 3-5 predicts whether a $1,400 crossbred calf lives, yet nobody independently verifies it at sale. Own that measurement and the warranty that follows.
customer: Calf raisers, backgrounders and feeder buyers who pay a premium for graded calves (or a subscription for the data), and dairies who pay to have calves graded so they can earn the premium. Later, insurers and MGAs underwriting a mortality warranty.
problem: Beef-on-dairy calf output went from about 50,000 head in 2014 to roughly 3.2M in 2024, with CattleFax projecting 5-6M, and calves have sold as high as $1,500 per head. Calf raisers buy 3-5 day old calves nearly blind and eat the 10-25% loss to scours and pneumonia. The colostrum information stays on the dairy, so raisers blame 'bad calves' and dairies blame 'bad luck'. Each dead calf now leaves a four-figure hole in a heifer pipeline that is short by hundreds of thousands of head.
solution: Independent serum total protein (Brix) testing on every calf at day 3-5, done at the dairy or at pickup by trained techs with digital refractometers and a phone app. Each calf is graded on the published four-tier passive-transfer scale (Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor) and logged with dairy, sire, weight and hydration score, then gets a QR tag or passport that follows the calf to the buyer. Buyers pay a premium for Excellent and Good and discount Poor. Phase 2 uses the accumulated data to price a 30- or 60-day mortality warranty ('we have graded 300,000 calves and know what a Brix 8.4 calf from Dairy X does'). Phase 3 gives dairies a colostrum scorecard that brokers use.
why_now: Crossbred calves are at record values, beef-on-dairy volume is doubling, and the heifer shortage means every lost calf is expensive and hard to replace. Consensus passive-transfer grading standards were published in 2020, digital refractometers are cheap, and buyers are already paying for verified genetics programs, so 'verified immunity' is the obvious next tag that nobody sells.
revenue_model: $4-6 per calf grading fee paid by the seller or split with the buyer, then $10-25 per calf warranty premium once loss data supports underwriting (partner with an insurer or MGA rather than carrying risk), plus a data subscription for larger calf raisers and feedlots.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone argues about sire genetics while the vet knows immune status dominates early death, and calves with failure of passive transfer carry about twice the risk of illness and death. The test is $1 and 60 seconds, but a number only has value when a neutral third party holds custody of it at the point of sale. The business is independent custody of the measurement, not the refractometer, and the resulting dataset becomes the underwriting moat.
first_30_days: Two vet techs, two $150 digital refractometers and a phone form. Offer free grading on 5 dairies' weekly calf shipments to 2-3 calf raisers or brokers. Ask the raiser to report 30-day illness and death by calf tag. After about 60 days, publish graded-versus-ungraded outcomes, then get one raiser to commit to a premium (for example $30-50) for Excellent calves and a discount for Poor, and charge the test fee from that point on.

title: Surge Beds: Pre-Contracted Lodging for Catastrophe Responders
one_liner: Sell adjuster firms and storm contractors reserved-bed options on inland RV pads, seasonal parks and closed motels, contracted before landfall at prices that stay legal after an emergency declaration.
customer: Independent-adjuster firms' cat operations and logistics managers, restoration franchisees, roofing and mitigation contractors bringing out-of-state crews, and utility subcontractors. Reservation fees are paid pre-season, activation nights after the event.
problem: After landfall or a big wildfire, responder capacity is limited by beds, not people. Adjusters sleep in cars, 90 minutes away, or in RVs on borrowed lots, and deployed adjusters quit or rotate out. Anti-gouging laws (34 states, typically capping increases at about 10% for 30 days after a declaration) stop hotels from raising rates, so price cannot allocate scarce rooms; they simply sell out to whoever had a relationship or a corporate block.
solution: A lodging-capacity option network. Sign inland owners 60-150 miles from likely landfall zones (seasonal RV parks and park-model communities that sit empty in hurricane season, church halls and school gyms, closed-for-season motels, dorms, and short-term-rental owners willing to accept 30-day minimum stays) to pre-agreed rates that are lawful because they were set before the emergency. Buyers pay a per-bed or per-site reservation fee before the season, credited against activation nights. Add paid extras that responders actually need: Starlink, laundry, catering, portable showers, secure parking for trucks and trailers. Extend to wildfire base camps in CA, OR and CO.
why_now: Quick searches surfaced no dedicated adjuster-lodging option marketplace, only ad hoc use of RV parks after storms like Michael. Two years of quiet U.S. hurricane landfalls (none in 2025, and no hurricane at all in the 2026 Atlantic season through Sept 11) mean firms have not tested surge logistics and will be caught out by the next big one. Adjuster and contractor headcounts are being squeezed by automation and tight margins, so a predictable per-bed cost is more attractive than scrambling. Anti-gouging enforcement has grown more aggressive.
revenue_model: Reservation fees of roughly $400-$900 per bed per season, credited against activation nights. On activation, a 15-20% margin over the pre-agreed owner rate, plus ancillary services (connectivity, meals, laundry) at 30-40% margin. Later, annual enterprise contracts with IA firms for guaranteed headcount blocks.
non_obvious_insight: Because gouging laws freeze price after the declaration, the only legal way to buy certainty is to contract early, which turns lodging into an options market where the option seller (a snowbird RV park empty from June to October) has almost no other use for its inventory in exactly the months responders need it. Insiders know the constraint on a cat deployment is where 200 adjusters sleep, not how many exist.
first_30_days: Call 50 seasonal RV parks, campgrounds and small motel owners across the inland Gulf Coast, Carolinas and Texas and sign non-binding LOIs on rates and bed counts. Draft a one-page option contract reviewed by a hospitality lawyer for gouging-law compliance. Pitch logistics managers at 8 IA firms and restoration franchise groups on 2027 pre-season blocks, aiming for 2-3 signed reservation deposits of 20-50 beds each. Build a simple booking and check-in app with texted access codes and a map of inventory.

title: Together Suites: Adjacent Units for Grandparent Care
one_liner: Lease linked or adjacent apartment pairs to a young family and a grandparent, with a fire-rated interior door where code allows, a relocation concierge, and help getting the grandparent paid through child care subsidy relative-care rules.
customer: Multifamily operators with adjacent vacant units in lease-up (bundle premium or per-lease fee), families and relocating grandparents (concierge fee), and state child care subsidy programs paying eligible relatives.
problem: Informal care by relatives is the largest unmeasured slice of care and no property software or policy tool manages it. Two kids in center care cost more than rent in every state. CCDF already pays relatives (about 67,900 relative caregivers received payments in FY2023, 27.5% of CCDF providers), but few families know it, and grandparents live far away. Operators sit on adjacent vacant units and give free months to fill them.
solution: 'Together Suites': two separate leases, one bundle, adjacent units with an interior door retrofit (roughly $4-8K where fire ratings allow) or same-corridor pairs where they do not. A concierge handles the grandparent's move, health plan and licensing details, and where the state allows it and the family qualifies, enrolls the grandparent as a paid relative provider with the required background check and training. A shared schedule app and a backup nanny pool cover gaps.
why_now: Lease-up glut and record concessions make adjacent vacant units cheap to commit. A record share of house hunters (18.7% in Q2 2026) are relocating, often for family or price. Relative-care rules are established and under-used.
revenue_model: Operator pays $100-150 a month per suite, or a lease-up bounty per bundle, funded by lower concessions and better retention. One-time concierge fee of $500-1,500 to families. Optional payroll and background-check margin.
non_obvious_insight: Informal care is the majority of care but invisible to real estate. An owner's oversupply of adjacent units is the cheapest childcare 'center' ever built, staffed by people who will do it for love plus a subsidy, and two linked households with a shared schedule almost never move out.
first_30_days: Pilot in one lease-up building with four to six adjacent vacant pairs. File the door-retrofit permit. Advertise through grandparent-relocation Facebook groups, pediatric offices and local parent groups. Sign two bundles and track lease-up time, concession spend, and subsidy approvals. Start in states where relatives can be paid with light requirements.

title: The Weekly Mail Box for Mom
one_liner: A prepaid return envelope where a parent drops all her mail. It gets scanned, triaged, shredded, and turned into a 'what needs doing' digest for her adult child.
customer: Adult children aged 45-62 with a parent 75+ living alone, often 100+ miles away. Secondary customers are daily money managers, professional fiduciaries and elder-law firms who currently collect and read mail by hand.
problem: Paper mail is where scams (fake invoices, 'prize fees', Medicare plan pitches), real bills and the notices that cost money arrive: property-tax exemption renewals, Part D changes, IRS notices, Medicaid paperwork. Kids discover the unopened shoebox at Thanksgiving. USPS Informed Delivery shows only the exterior of some letter-size mail. Parents refuse apps, dashboards and shared passwords because that feels like surrender.
solution: A weekly pre-addressed return flat that the parent fills with the whole pile, with no sorting. The team scans it, uses AI to classify and extract sender, amount, due date and required action, flags likely scams (any 'send a check to claim your prize' letter), and calls or texts the parent for urgent items ('Do you want the water bill paid?'). The child gets a weekly digest and a dashboard. Originals are shredded or returned monthly, per the parent's choice. Over time it builds the 'where everything is' paper trail that estates need: accounts, policies, pensions and annuities.
why_now: Cheap, accurate AI document extraction only became affordable at consumer prices in the last two years. Treasury phased out paper checks on Sept 30, 2025, and agencies are pushing digital, while seniors still get paper notices. Older-adult scam losses run in the billions per year (FTC). Medicare open enrollment begins Oct 15, so the mailer flood is imminent.
revenue_model: $49/month per household (about $14 in postage, scanning and AI, for roughly 70% gross margin). $25 per household per month wholesale for daily money managers and fiduciaries. Optional $149 one-time 'estate paper trail' report.
non_obvious_insight: Seniors will turn down every dashboard, but they will hand over an envelope pile happily, because mailing is a ritual they own. The pile is the real system of record for a widow's finances. Scam checks and wire requests are usually triggered by letters, so scanning the inside of the envelope catches what exterior-only tools cannot. Children do not want passwords either. They want to know what to pay.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 households in one metro through caregiver Facebook groups, local AARP caregiver meetings and elder-law attorneys. Run it manually with a $500 duplex scanner, an AI extraction pipeline and a retired teacher doing quality checks. Charge from day one. Track 'catches' (scams intercepted, missed notices found) and publish them. Then pitch daily money managers.

title: Tariff Surcharge Clawback for B2B Buyers
one_liner: A contingency-fee service that mines a buyer's 2025-26 supplier invoices for 'tariff surcharge' lines and recovers a share of the IEEPA refunds those suppliers are now collecting.
customer: Multi-unit restaurant and retail franchisees, contractor purchasing co-ops, and mid-market distributors' customers that paid itemized tariff, freight or 'inflation' surcharges to suppliers who were the importer of record. They pay a 20-30% success fee on money recovered.
problem: IEEPA duty refunds go only to the importer of record (IOR) or a party the IOR designates. Buyers who paid the tariff as a surcharge or a higher price get nothing unless they ask. AutoZone booked about $96M and Cracker Barrel $15M, with MillerKnoll $16.5M and Worthington $4M. Downstream buyers have no visibility into what their suppliers recovered and no process to ask for it.
solution: Read-only inbox and AP connectors pull 2025-26 invoices and extract surcharge, 'tariff', 'duty' and 'trade cost recovery' line items. The system estimates each supplier's IEEPA exposure from public import-manifest data. It checks the supplier's terms for pass-back language, such as 'surcharge will be removed or refunded if tariffs are rescinded'. It then generates a claim letter with an offer to accept credit memos or to have the supplier name the buyer as the CBP Form 4811 notify party so the refund routes to the buyer. A second module audits new diesel and fuel surcharges against the contract formula and the EIA diesel index. Claims are sent to the top 20 suppliers per buyer, and unclaimed money is tracked to closure.
why_now: CBP's CAPE portal opened in 2026 and is issuing refunds within 60-90 days of an accepted declaration. Refunds are landing in Q3-Q4 2026 P&Ls as one-time gains. Suppliers are least defensible in the first months after booking a windfall and will negotiate to keep customer goodwill. Diesel is $6.53/gal, up $2.78 year over year, so a wave of fresh surcharge invoices is arriving that nobody audits.
revenue_model: A 20-30% contingency fee on recovered refunds and credits, plus $199-$999/month for continuous surcharge auditing (fuel, energy, 'regulatory recovery' fees) once the first recovery lands.
non_obvious_insight: The refund windfall is a transfer from customers to importers, and the CFOs say so. AutoZone's CFO said 'the refund environment was deflationary, and the industry likely would have raised prices faster if both retailers and suppliers hadn't received cost relief' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/22/autozone-azo-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Cracker Barrel booked a $15M refund and MillerKnoll $16.5M, worth 180 bps of gross margin (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/23/cracker-barrel-cbrl-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/ and https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/22/mlkn-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). CBP states 'Only the IOR ... or the authorized customs broker ... may file' and never mentions downstream buyers, couriers or DDP shipments (https://www.cbp.gov/trade/programs-administration/trade-remedies/ieepa-duty-refunds). Every downstream claim is therefore a negotiation, and the buyer who holds the 2025 invoices has the leverage. Nobody is selling that to the buyer side. The legal caveat is that the buyer needs an explicit surcharge line or contract language to have a real claim, so the product should target only those cases.
first_30_days: Recruit 5-8 restaurant franchisee groups or contractor purchasing co-ops through franchisee associations and buying-group managers, with a free 'we only get paid if you get paid' offer. Export 2025 AP data or forward invoice PDFs, then have an analyst plus an LLM extraction script build a surcharge ledger for the top 15 suppliers each. Send the first 30 claim letters with a one-page template that cites the refund program and asks for credit or 4811 routing. Have a supply-chain lawyer review the template. Aim to close the first paid recovery within 60-75 days.

title: Hotel Strike Early-Warning for Event Planners
one_liner: A subscription database and parametric cover that tells meeting and group planners which contracted hotels' labour contracts expire before their event, and pays out if a strike hits.
customer: Association and corporate meeting planners, incentive houses, sports and event organisers and tour operators that contract 100+ room-night blocks 12-24 months ahead.
problem: Chicago hotel workers authorised a strike at 85%, potentially the largest in the city's history, and a Seattle Hilton strike lasted 85 days. Planners contract blocks years ahead and learn about labour risk from the news. Strike coverage under contract clauses is vague, and relocating an event on short notice costs heavily.
solution: Track union contract expirations, strike votes and bargaining status per property, from union pages, filings and news. Score each hotel and date for strike risk, alert planners, and provide a labour-disruption clause template. Later add parametric cover underwritten by an MGA that pays per room-night if a strike affects a contracted property.
why_now: Hotel labour unrest is elevated in 2026, hotel costs have repriced sharply, and hotel operators are cutting staff citing AI (Mews cut 15%). Planners are more exposed to relocation than ever.
revenue_model: USD 3-8K per year per planning team, cover premiums of about 1.5-3% of block value, and broker fees.
non_obvious_insight: A strike is a scheduled event, not a surprise. Contract expiry dates are public, yet the buyers of long-dated blocks bear the tail risk and nobody prices it.
first_30_days: Compile a spreadsheet of union contract expirations for the top 40 US convention cities from union local sites and news. Publish a free '2027 events at risk' report to planner communities, then convert responders to a USD 2K annual subscription. Line up an MGA for the cover after the first 10 customers.

title: Referee Body-Cams and Abuse Evidence Layer
one_liner: A clip-on camera and incident-report service that gives youth and high school officials proof and gives leagues grounds to ban abusive spectators.
customer: State high school associations, officials' associations, youth leagues and tournament operators, paying per official per season.
problem: About 50,000 high school officials have left since 2018, more than 70 percent of new referees quit within three years, and half report feeling unsafe. Insiders assume pay raises fix the shortage, but abuse is the driver and leagues cannot sanction parents or coaches without evidence, so games run short-staffed or get cancelled.
solution: A $50-100 chest-mounted camera or phone clip with audio; speech-to-text flags threats and slurs; league admins get a one-click incident packet (timestamps, transcript, clip) tied to a spectator code of conduct; officials get a private 'safe report' button. Leagues use the evidence to issue bans and support refs.
why_now: 2026 shortage coverage (New York, Utah and others) consistently blames abuse; cheap on-device transcription and body cams make this a $60 problem; national bodies such as USA Volleyball have created formal harassment-response programs, showing appetite.
revenue_model: $40-90 per official per season (hardware included) plus $500-3k per year per league for the admin dashboard; potential insurer partnerships.
non_obvious_insight: The shortage is a safety problem, not a pay problem, and the true buyer is the league's risk manager. Recording laws vary by state, so the product is policy-first (posted notices, opt-in associations) and starts where the association mandates it.
first_30_days: Pilot with one regional officials association (about 100 officials) using off-the-shelf action cams and a transcription pipeline, draft a spectator-policy template with a local attorney, run one season of evidence, and convert two leagues into paying customers.

title: Auto-to-Defense Conversion Accelerator for Tier-2 Suppliers
one_liner: A fixed-price certification package plus matched RFQs that turn idle auto-parts plants into qualified defense and aerospace suppliers.
customer: Tier-2 and tier-3 automotive stampers, machiners and casting shops with 25-250 employees in the Midwest and South. Defense primes co-fund supplier development.
problem: OEM robot orders are down 25% and autos lost 4.5k jobs in August, while defense money is flowing (Hadrian raised $1.37B; it holds an $80M Army deal). Auto suppliers have capacity and process discipline (IATF), but defense work needs AS9100, ITAR registration, DFARS specialty-metals tracking and NIST 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 (phase 2 is scheduled for November 2026). Consultants sell these piecemeal.
solution: A 90-day package: gap assessment, IATF-to-AS9100 crosswalk, ITAR registration, an NIST 800-171 plan on a managed enclave, DFARS specialty-metals tracking, and a mock audit, delivered mostly by templates and a small compliance team. It ends with RFQs matched from primes looking for capacity.
why_now: The auto retreat leaves capacity idle, defense capital is at record levels, and CMMC requirements are phasing in. Primes need more sub-tier suppliers.
revenue_model: $35-80k fixed fee per shop or $3-5k a month for the managed enclave. Success fee on first contract. RFQ-routing fees from primes.
non_obvious_insight: Auto suppliers already have the hard part (process discipline, volume) but are invisible to primes for lack of paperwork. Selling capacity conversion instead of compliance opens the prime's supplier-development budget. The CMMC consultant market is crowded, so the wedge is the RFQ match, not the audit.
first_30_days: Recruit five shops through chambers of commerce, auto-supplier associations and state MEP centers. Partner with a C3PAO and a GCC High MSP. Meet two primes' supplier-development teams about co-funding. Land two paid pilots at about $25k.

title: WhatsApp Tandas With Credit Reporting
one_liner: Felix proved WhatsApp-native finance at $8B of volume. Wrap the rotating savings groups that immigrant households already run in group chats with escrow, default cover and credit reporting.
customer: Latino, West African, Caribbean and South Asian households running tandas, susus and chit-fund-style rotating savings groups. The FDIC's 2023 survey counts 5.6M unbanked and 19M underbanked households, with minimum balances the top barrier.
problem: Rotating savings groups are the real financial system for many households, but they run on cash and trust, one bad organizer or defaulter breaks the pot, and the on-time payment history is invisible to credit bureaus. Cash-funded remittances now carry a 1% federal tax, nudging cash economies toward digital.
solution: A WhatsApp bot to create a tanda (amounts, order, schedule). Contributions are held in a partner-bank pass-through balance, or in stablecoin where appropriate, and payouts release on schedule. The organizer earns a fee, and a small guarantee pool covers late payers. On-time contributions are reported to bureaus as installment history through a furnisher partner.
why_now: Felix reached $8B cumulative volume with revenue up 2.5x on WhatsApp, the remittance tax pushes cash users to digital rails (Forbes, 2026-07-17), and stablecoin and bank-partner rails make small-balance escrow cheap.
revenue_model: 1-2% fee on each pot, $5 per month credit-building subscription, and lender referral fees for graduated members.
non_obvious_insight: Don't replace the tanda, wrap it. The organizer is a trusted social underwriter with better default data than any bureau. The pooled payment history of organized groups becomes a proprietary dataset lenders will pay for.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 organizers via Spanish-language WhatsApp and Facebook groups, churches, taquerias and community organizations. Run 10 pilot tandas with manual escrow in a partner-bank sub-account at a 1.5% fee, and validate the credit-reporting path with a furnisher.
